clue.text: It makes him cry, dope injected, under the skin

indicators.note: dope injected into the patient is mixed in, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A needle full of dope pushed into the skin makes the patient wince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' signals mixing the letters of HIM CRY and DOPE together; 'It makes' is just a link, though the surface hints that the needle is what makes one cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypodermic, as an adjective, describes something lying or given beneath the dermis, as an injection is.

clue.text: Endless bliss, to have a fling!

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the bliss word

parts.note: heaven is a state of bliss

explanation.surface: Someone in endless bliss enjoys a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fling' looks like a romance, but here a fling is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to hurl or throw something heavy.

clue.text: Urge the, president to provide early transport

parts.note: to push is to urge
a chair is the president of a meeting

explanation.surface: Lobbying the president for transport early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early transport' means transport early in life, a baby's buggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby buggy carries a child in the first years of life.

clue.text: Fold the flag? It's a discriminatory rule

parts.note: to double something is to fold it over
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: Is folding the national flag an unfair regulation?
explanation.definitionFit: A principle applied more strictly to some people than others is unfair and biased.

clue.text: Effects a revolution in the management of crops?

explanation.surface: Something that brings about a revolution in farming.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is spinning round; the second is the farmer's practice of changing crops in a field each season.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning on an axis is literal revolution; and farmers alternate which crops grow in each field.

clue.text: More positive support for trendy underwriter

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits below the word it holds up

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A more confident backer of a fashionable insurance company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for' puts SURER under IN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter is a company that takes on risk in return for a premium.

clue.text: Source of record return for leaders of cinema industry?

definitions.text: Source of record return for leaders of cinema industry?

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: return means the picked letters come back in the opposite order
leaders of the words cinema and industry are their first letters

explanation.surface: Film bosses wonder what will bring record box-office returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the initials C and I, from 'leaders of', into IC after EP. The whole clue also defines: a lavish big-screen spectacle is what earns studios record takings.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand historical film spectacle is the kind of blockbuster that brings film studios huge takings.

clue.text: Paying guest a boy at heart? You have a point

indicators.note: at heart means the boy's name sits in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lodger who is a lad underneath has a valid argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You have a point' suggests agreement, but the definition is a sharp tine.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is one spike or tine of a fork.

clue.text: Have tea, if brewed with uncommon care here

definitions.text: Have tea, if brewed with uncommon care here

indicators.note: brewed suggests stirring things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Take your tea here, made with unusual attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' (with 'uncommon' reinforcing it) mixes TEA, IF and CARE; the whole clue then describes a self-service café, where tea is rarely made with care.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is where you might drink your tea.

clue.text: Bird, brings, information about old rustic outside: Hindhead

indicators.note: about means the information word goes around the other piece

parts.note: gen is slang for information
taken as written

indicators.note: outside means the rustic word wraps around the following letter

parts.note: a peasant is a rustic country person
read as hind head: the head of hind is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird brings news about an old countryman near the Surrey village of Hindhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Hindhead is a village in Surrey, England; split as 'Hind head' it gives the first letter of hind.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured game bird of Chinese origin, often kept for its golden plumage.

clue.text: An old sailor heard this attack

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is to be said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: an old sailor is a salt, so the phrase gives A SALT

explanation.surface: Someone listening to a veteran seaman tells of an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' tells you to say A SALT (an old sailor) out loud: it sounds like the word for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent onslaught, a synonym for an attack.

clue.text: Proudly demonstrate effect of " players' strike

explanation.surface: A boastful display is what happens when actors walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: If the players go on strike, the show is off: read the phrase literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to parade it proudly; and an actors' walkout means the performance is cancelled.

clue.text: It helps to move many a line in a store, perhaps

definitions.text: It helps to move many a line in a store, perhaps

parts.words: It helps to move many a line in a store, perhaps
parts.note: suggests selling stock lines, but means a moving staircase carrying a line of shoppers between floors

explanation.surface: Something that helps a shop shift lots of its product lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move many a line' sounds like selling goods, but the line is of people being carried up a shop's moving stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Department stores use moving staircases to lift queues of customers from floor to floor.

clue.text: An under-ten making a sly remark, it appears

parts.note: a dig is a pointed or sly remark

explanation.surface: A child under ten seems to be making a cheeky comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An under-ten' sounds like a young child, but it means any number from nought to nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral runs from 0 to 9, so every one is below ten.

clue.text: Celebrities seen, possibly, after suffering 10

explanation.surface: Famous people are spotted after being beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is ASSAULT: after a blow to the head you may 'see' little points of light, the cartoon sight of dazed victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous performers are called by the name of shining heavenly bodies; and dizzy lights are what a struck person sees.

clue.text: King, much appreciated over the years

explanation.surface: A monarch beloved through the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the British gold coin, which has risen greatly in value.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a ruling head of state; the gold coin has gained in value as bullion.

clue.text: A. Democrat in, calmer surroundings, playing his guitar?.

indicators.note: calmer surroundings means the calmer word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: serener means more calm
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American Democrat relaxes in peaceful settings with a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' places A and D inside SERENER. The definition describes a person by what he does: strumming under a balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooing musician strums beneath a window at night, often on a guitar or lute.

clue.text: He may engrave and colour, say, an angler's weight

indicators.note: say means the colour word is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: to dye is to colour
a sinker is the weight on a fishing line

explanation.surface: A craftsman who engraves and paints, perhaps an angler too.
explanation.walkthrough: A die-sinker engraves the dies used to stamp coins and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: This craftsman cuts designs into metal stamps for striking coins.

clue.text: Many-talented, producing poems out of a hat, almost

indicators.note: the poems word is placed out around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: verse means poems collectively

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the hat word is dropped

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A gifted conjuror pulls poems from a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TILE (slang for a hat) to TIL; with A it sits inside VERSE, which 'out of' places around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile describes someone adaptable, with a wide range of skills.

clue.text: Barbarous as man 'is to man, Burns thought

definitions.text: Barbarous as man 'is to man, Burns thought

parts.words: Barbarous as man 'is to man, Burns thought
parts.note: alludes to Robert Burns's line about man's cruelty to man, the quality the clue describes

explanation.surface: Robert Burns thought men were barbarous to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns wrote 'Man's inhumanity to man makes countless thousands mourn' in 'Man was made to Mourn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous behaviour lacks compassion, the cruelty Burns lamented in men.

clue.text: Honour Ben and Leon for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ben and Leon are honoured for once.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise to the peerage is to honour someone with a title.

clue.text: He's always spotted -if he's laughing

parts.note: reads like a person who is noticed when amused, but describes the spotted and laughing varieties of an African scavenger

explanation.surface: A jolly man can always be noticed by his laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' means having spots, not noticed; the laughing kind is named for its cackling call.
explanation.definitionFit: The African scavenging carnivore has spotted and laughing varieties.

clue.text: Moving quickly and quietly in surprise attack

indicators.note: in means the quietly letter is placed inside the attack word

parts.note: a raid is a surprise attack
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Commandos move fast and silently during a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means swift, describing something that goes fast.

clue.text: A piece of sculpture to place. above it

indicators.note: in this down entry the place word sits above the word to

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: Instructions to position a sculpture over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above it' puts PUT on top of TO in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a cherub figure in Renaissance art and sculpture.

clue.text: One in central Europe executed a heretic

parts.note: hung means put to death on the gallows
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: Someone in central Europe put a heretic to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a heretic' gives ARIAN, a follower of Arius, not the racial term.
explanation.definitionFit: A Magyar native lives in a landlocked country of central Europe.

clue.text: Notorious book-lined study turned upside down

indicators.note: book-lined means the book letters line the inside of the study
in this down entry the study word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a private study
OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A notorious study full of books has been ransacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned upside down' flips DEN to NED; 'lined' puts OT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known, which notorious also means, though usually for bad reasons.

clue.text: Bury that cockney chap in the meantime

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a Londoner drops the H, so 'him' becomes 'im

explanation.surface: Bury that East End fellow while waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop initial H, so 'him' becomes IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim, as an adverbial phrase, means for the time being.

clue.text: Support for a group falling. within defined limits

definitions.text: a group falling. within defined limits

explanation.surface: Help for a group that falls inside set boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: A shelf support is one sense; the other is a band such as an age or tax band.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall fixture holds up a shelf; and a category between two limits, like an income band, is the second sense.

clue.text: Japanese drama acceptable in retreat

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A Japanese play is acceptable in a quiet retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded corner or recess is a place to withdraw to.

clue.text: A Frenchman, without character and lacking education

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with no personality and no schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: A Frenchman would say UN for 'a'; read with LETTERED it is 'un-lettered', without letters or characters, which is also the literal sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never learned to read or write is illiterate; literally the word means having no alphabet characters.
